In mathematics, the '''tribonacci ratio''' is a  geometrical [[aspect ratio|proportion]], given by the unique real [[polynomial root|solution]] of the equation {{nowrap|{{math|1=''x''{{isup|3}} = ''x''{{isup|2}} + ''x'' + 1}}.}} Its decimal expansion begins with {{math|{{val|1.839286755214161|end=...}} }} {{OEIS|A058265}}.<!-- PLEASE DO NOT add additional digits to the value of τ in this equation; there is a long-standing consensus that additional digits do not add to understanding. Thank you.-->

The moniker ''tribonacci'' was introduced by high-school student Mark Feinberg in an article published in the ''[[Fibonacci Quarterly]]'' of october 1963.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Feinberg |first=Mark |title=Fibonacci-Tribonacci |url=https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/1-3/feinberg.pdf |journal=[[Fibonacci Quarterly]] |volume=1 | issue=3 |pages=71–74 |date=October 1963 |doi=10.1080/00150517.1963.12431573}}</ref>

==Definition==
[[File:Tribonacci cuboid.svg |thumb |upright=1.25 |{{math|1=τ = {{sfrac|a+b+c|a}} = {{sfrac|a|b}} = {{sfrac|b|c}} }}. With {{math|1=b = 1}} the boxes have volumes {{math|1=τ{{isup|3}} = τ{{isup|2}} (red) + τ (green) + 1 (blue).}}]]

Three quantities {{math|a > b > c > 0}} are in the tribonacci ratio if
<math display="block"> \frac{a+b+c}{a} =\frac{a}{b} =\frac{b}{c} =\tau</math>
This ratio is commonly denoted {{tmath|\tau.}}

Substituting {{tmath|1=b =\tau c}} and {{tmath|1=a =\tau b =\tau^2 c}} in the first fraction gives
<math display=block>\tau =\frac{c(\tau^2 +\tau +1)}{\tau^2 c}.</math> It follows that the tribonacci ratio is the unique real solution of the [[cubic equation]] <math>\tau^3 =\tau^2 +\tau +1</math>.

Closed-form expressions for {{tmath|\tau}} are found by solving the [[depressed cubic]] {{tmath| y^3 -\tfrac43 y -\tfrac{38}{27} }}, which has real zero {{tmath|\tau -\tfrac13}}.<ref>{{OEIS|A058265}}</ref>
<math display="block"> \begin{align}
 w_{1,2} &=19 \pm 3\sqrt{33} \\
 \tau &=\left(1 +\sqrt[3]{w_1} +\sqrt[3]{w_2} \right) /3 \\
 &= \frac13 +\frac43 \cosh \left( \frac13 \operatorname{arcosh} \left( \frac{19}{8} \right) \right).
\end{align}</math>

Dividing the defining polynomial {{tmath|z^3 -z^2 -z -1}} by {{tmath|z -\tau}} one obtains {{tmath|z^2 +(\tau -1)z +1 /\tau}}, and the [[Conjugate element (field theory)|conjugate elements]] of {{tmath|\tau}} are
<math display=block>z_{1,2} = \left( 1 -\tau \pm i \sqrt{(\tau +1)(3\tau -5)} \right) /2 ,</math>
with {{tmath|1=z_1 +z_2 =1 -\tau}} and {{tmath|1=z_1 z_2 =1 /\tau}}.

[[File:Tribonacci_definition.svg |thumb |Unit circle and hyperbola {{math|1=(''x'' + 1) ''y'' = 1}}.]]
The point of intersection {{tmath|1=P =(x,y)}} with {{tmath| x \ne 0}} of [[unit circle]] <math> x^2 +y^2 =1 </math> and [[Hyperbola#Rectangular hyperbola|rectangular hyperbola]] <math> y =\frac{1}{x+1} </math> is {{tmath| (\tau -1,\tau^{-1}).}} Substituting for {{tmath|y}}, the equation of the [[Abscissa and ordinate|abscissa]] is <math>\, x^3 +2x^2 -2 =0 \,</math> or <math>\, x^2 (x +2) =2.</math>

Dividing both sides by {{tmath|\, x+2}} results in the [[Fixed-point iteration|fixed point]] iteration <math>\, x_{n+1} \gets \sqrt{ \frac{2}{2 +x_n} } \,,</math> and the continued reciprocal square root
<math display=block> \tau -1 =\sqrt{\cfrac{2}{2+\sqrt{\cfrac{2}{2+\sqrt{\cfrac{2}{2 +\ddots}}}}}} </math>
An image of the Julia set of the backward iteration <math>\, z_{n-1} \gets \frac{2}{z^2_n} -2 \,</math> in the complex plane is found [[#Bells|below]].

Alternative expressions for the tribonacci ratio are derived from the [[Reciprocal polynomial|reciprocal equation]], that is, the depressed cubic {{tmath|\, 2x^3 -2x -1 \,}} with real zero {{tmath|\frac{1}{\tau-1} }} and [[discriminant]] {{tmath|-44}}.<ref>{{OEIS|A316711}} − 1</ref>
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 w_{1,2} &=\left( 1 \pm \frac13 \sqrt{ \frac{11}{3}} \right) /4 \\
 \tau &=1 +(\sqrt[3]{w_1} +\sqrt[3]{w_2})^{-1} \\
 &= 1 +\frac{\sqrt3}{2} \operatorname{sech}\left( \frac13 \operatorname{arcosh} \left( \frac{3\sqrt3}{4} \right) \right).
\end{align}</math>

Additionally, <math>\, 2x^3 =2x +1 \,</math> leads to the [[Nested radical#Infinitely nested radicals|infinite radical]]
<math display=block> \frac{1}{\tau-1} =\sqrt[3]{\tfrac12 +\sqrt[3]{\tfrac12 +\sqrt[3]{\tfrac12 +\cdots}}}</math>

{{tmath|\frac{1}{\tau-1} }} is the [[Stability theory#Stability of fixed points|superstable]] fixed point of the [[Newton's method|Newton iteration]] {{tmath|x \gets (2x^3 +\tfrac12) /(3x^2 -1)}}.

==Properties==
[[File:TribonacciSquare_6.svg |thumb |upright=1.2 |Rectangles with aspect ratios {{math|{{sfrac|1|τ−1}}, τ, {{sfrac|τ|τ−1}} }} tile the square.]]
The tribonacci ratio can be written in terms of itself as fractions
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \tau &=\frac{\tau^2 +1}{\tau^2 -1} \\
 \tau^2 &=\frac{\tau +1}{\tau -1} \\
 \tau^3 &=\frac{\tau^4 +1}{2} \\
 \tau^4 &=\frac{\,(\tau +1)^3}{2}.\end{align}</math>

Similarly as the infinite [[geometric series]]
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \frac{\tau^2 +1}{2} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \tau^{-n} \\
 \frac{\tau +1}{2} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \tau^{-2n} \\
 \frac{1}{\tau -1} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \tau^{-3n} \\
 \frac{\tau}{2(\tau -1)} &=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \tau^{-4n}.\end{align}</math>

For every integer {{tmath|n}} one has
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \tau^n &=\tau^{n-1} +\tau^{n-2} +\tau^{n-3} \\
 &=2\tau^{n-2} +2\tau^{n-3} +\tau^{n-4} \\
 &=3\tau^{n-2} +\tau^{n-4} +\tau^{n-6}
\end{align}</math>
from this an infinite number of further relations can be found. A notable example is {{tmath|1=\tau +\tau^{-3} =2}}.

[[Simple continued fraction|Continued fraction]] pattern of a few low powers&nbsp;<ref>For τ {{OEIS|A019712}}</ref>
<math display=block>\begin{align}
 \tau^{-1} &=[0;1,1,5,4,2,305,1,8,2,...] \approx 0.5437 \;(\tfrac{31}{57}) \\
 \tau^0 &=[1] \\
 \tau^1 &=[1;1,5,4,2,305,1,8,2,1,...] \approx 1.8393 \;(\tfrac{103}{56}) \\
 \tau^2 &=[3;2,1,1,1,1,2,1,152,2,...] \approx 3.3830 \;(\tfrac{159}{47}) \\
 \tau^3 &=[6;4,2,305,1,8,2,1,4,6,...] \approx 6.2223 \;(\tfrac{56}{9}) \\
 \tau^4 &=[11;2,4,152,1,17,1,2,2,...] \approx 11.4445 \;(\tfrac{103}{9})
\end{align}</math>

The tribonacci ratio is the fourth smallest cubic [[Pisot number]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Panju |first=Maysum |date=2011 |title=A systematic construction of almost integers |url=https://mathreview.uwaterloo.ca/archive/voli/2/panju.pdf |journal=The Waterloo Mathematics Review |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=35–43 |access-date=August 15, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> By definition of these numbers, the [[Absolute value#Complex numbers|absolute value]] <math>1 /\sqrt{\tau}</math> of the algebraic conjugates is smaller than 1, thus powers of {{tmath|\tau}} generate [[almost integer]]s.
For example: <math> \tau^{18} =58034.99919...</math> {{tmath|\approx 58035 -1/1234}}. After 18 rotation steps the [[Phase (waves)|phase]]s of the inward spiraling conjugate pair &ndash; initially close to {{tmath| \pm 9\pi /13}} &ndash; nearly align with the imaginary axis.

The first implied mention of the tribonacci constant was in the eleventh century, when the Persian poet and [[polymath]] [[Omar Khayyam]] found the solution {{tmath|10\tfrac{\tau+1}{\tau} }} of the cubic <math>x^3 +200x =20x^2 +2000</math> by considering the intersection of a circle and a rectangular hyperbola.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lang |first=Wolfdieter |date=2015 |title=A geometrical problem of Omar Khayyám and its cubic |url=https://oeis.org/A256099/a256099_1.pdf |website=[[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] |access-date=2026-06-30}}</ref>

<math>W_{11}(x) = x^3 -2x^2 +2x -2,</math> with real zero <math>\omega =\tfrac{\tau+1}{\tau} =\tau(\tau -1),</math> is the [[Weber modular function|Weber class polynomial]] associated with discriminant {{tmath|1=\Delta=-11}}. Properties of the related [[J-invariant#The q-expansion and moonshine|Klein j-invariant]] result in near-identity <math>\omega \approx (e^{\pi \sqrt{-\Delta}} +24)^{1/24}.</math>

[https://math.deweger.net/reports/%5b1999%5dBroberg.txt Benne de Weger's example] for the algebraic [[abc conjecture]] derives from the [[Fibonacci_sequence#Binet's_formula |Binet-type expression]] for the zero element at index {{math|52}} of the Berstel sequence.<ref>{{OEIS|A007420}}</ref> The [[Linear recurrence with constant coefficients#Definitions |companion polynomial]] to the recurrence relation is <math> x^3 -2x^2 +4x -4 </math>, with real zero <math> \alpha =2\tfrac{\tau}{\tau +1}</math>.

[[File:TRIBONACCI.jpg |thumb |upright=1.25 |Construction of the tribonacci ratio with compass and marked ruler. {{math|1=BC = τ − 1}} and {{math|1=BD = {{sfrac|1|τ}} }}.]]
Argument <math> \theta =\arccos(\tfrac12 \tau) \,</math> satisfies <math>\, 4\sin(3\theta) -\tan(\theta) =\sqrt{11} </math>, a result which is related through distance parameter <math>\, z =\tau(1 -\tau) \cdot 2\cos(\tfrac{2\pi}{11}) </math> to the 'miraculous' [[neusis construction]] of the [[hendecagon]], found by Benjamin and Snyder.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lanzi |first=Oscar |date=Jun 11, 2019 |title=Trig identities analogous to tan(pi/5) + 4sin(pi/5) = sqrt(5 + 2sqrt(5)) |url=https://math.stackexchange.com/q/3258069 |website=Mathematics stack exchange |access-date=2026-07-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benjamin |first1=Elliot |last2=Snyder |first2=Chip |title=On the construction of the regular hendecagon by marked ruler and compass |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262991453_On_the_construction_of_the_regular_hendecagon_by_marked_ruler_and_compass |journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]] |volume=156 |issue=3 |date=May 2014 |pages=409-424 |doi=10.1017/S0305004113000753}}</ref>

The reciprocal {{tmath|\tfrac{1}{\tau} }} of the tribonacci ratio solves the equation <math>\, 2\arctan(x) =\arccos(x)</math>.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chema |first=Peter M. |date=2017 |title=Tribonacci constant as ratio of square to rhombus projection |url=https://oeis.org/A058265/a058265_2.pdf |website=[[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] |access-date=2026-06-30}}</ref> The angle is close to {{math|1}} [[radian]]. Its [[Angle#Complementary angle|complement]] <math>\, \arccos(\tau-1) =\arcsin(\tfrac{1}{\tau}) \,</math> figures in the geometric construction of the tribonacci constant found by biologist Xerardo Neira.<ref>{{cite web |last=Neira |first=Xerardo |date=Dec 12, 2020 |title=A geometric construction of the tribonacci constant with marked ruler and compass |url=https://oeis.org/A058265/a058265_3.pdf |website=[[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] |access-date=2026-06-30}}</ref>

The tribonacci ratio is particularly important in the study of the [[snub cube]]: all its metrics can be expressed in terms of {{tmath|\tau}}.

==Tribonacci sequence==
The first muddled mention of the tribonacci sequence is in [[Charles Darwin]]'s ''[[On the Origin of Species]]'' (1859), illustrating the population growth of elephants on the supposition that during their lifetime each pair of parents produces three pair of young.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Podani |first1=János |last2=Kun |first2=Ádám |last3=Szilágyi |first3=András |title=How Fast Does Darwin's Elephant Population Grow? |url=http://real.mtak.hu/72652/1/Podani_etal_DarwinElephants.pdf |journal=Journal of the History of Biology |volume=51 |issue=2 |pages=259–281 |year=2018 |doi=10.1007/s10739-017-9488-5}}</ref>

The number of [[Composition (combinatorics)|compositions]] of {{math|''n'' − 2}} into parts 1, 2 and 3 is counted by the ''n''th tribonacci number ({{math|''n'' > 1}}).

The tribonacci sequence is defined by the third-order [[recurrence relation]]
<math display=block>T_n =T_{n-1} +T_{n-2} +T_{n-3} \text{ for } n >2,</math>
with initial values
<math display=block>T_0 =T_1 =0, T_2 =1.</math>

The first few terms are 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44, 81, 149, 274, 504, 927,... {{OEIS|A000073}}.{{br}}
The limit ratio between consecutive terms is the tribonacci constant:<math>\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} T_{n+1}/T_n =\tau.</math>{{br}}
An alternative relation for {{tmath|n >3}} is given by <math>T_n =2T_{n-1} -T_{n-4}.</math>

The sequence is extended to negative indices using
<math display=block> T_n =T_{n+3} -T_{n+2} -T_{n+1},</math>
obtaining (0), 1,−1, 0, 2,−3, 1, 4,−8, 5, 7,−20, 18, 9,−47,... {{OEIS|A057597}}.

The relationship between the negative and positive indexed segments of the sequence is given by
<math display=block> T_{1-n} =T_n^2 - T_{n+1} T_{n-1}.</math>
This [[reflection formula]] holds for all integers {{tmath|n}} and can be derived from Agronomof's identity&nbsp;<ref>{{cite journal |last=Agronomof |first=Nicolai A. |title=Sur une suite récurrente |journal=Mathesis |volume=4 |pages=125–126 |year=1914 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Tuenter |first=Hans J. H. |title=In Search of Comrade Agronomof: Some Tribonacci History |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=130 |issue=8 |pages=708–719 |date=October 2023 |doi = 10.1080/00029890.2023.2231796 |mr=4645497 |zbl=1527.01024}}</ref>
<math display=block> T_{n+k} = T_{k+1} T_{n+1} + \left(T_k +T_{k-1} \right) T_n + T_k T_{n-1}.</math>

The sequence is related to sums of [[binomial coefficient]]s by
<math display=block> T_{n+2} =\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \sum_{j=0}^{i} {i \choose j}{n-i-j \choose i} </math>

<span class="anchor" id="Bells">[[File:Tribonacci_Bells.jpg |thumb |upright=1.25 |Julia set (in black) of the map {{math|z ← {{sfrac|2|z{{sup|2}} }} − 2}} with a single attracting, real five-point limit cycle. Viewport width {{math|[−3,3]}}, pole {{math|1=z{{sub|p}} = 0}}. The tiny white circle is centred at repelling fixed point {{math|1=z{{sub|f}} = τ − 1}}.]]</span>
Powers of the tribonacci ratio can be written with tribonacci numbers as quadratic coefficients <math display=block> \tau^n =\tau^2 T_{n} +\tau (T_{n-1} +T_{n-2}) +T_{n-1},</math> which is proved by [[mathematical induction]] on {{tmath|n.}} This relation also holds for {{tmath|n < 0.}} The order of the coefficients corresponds to the bottom row of matrix {{tmath|Q}} below.

The [[generating function]] of the tribonacci sequence for non-negative {{math|''n''}} is given by
<math display=block>\frac{x^2}{1 -x -x^2 -x^3} =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} T_n x^n \text{ for } x <\tfrac{1}{\tau}</math>

Let {{tmath|\tau}} and [[Conjugate element (field theory)|complex conjugate]] pair {{tmath|\beta}} and {{tmath|\gamma}} be the zeros of polynomial {{tmath|f:x^3 -x^2 -x -1}} with [[discriminant]] {{tmath|-44}}, the tribonacci numbers are then given by the [[Fibonacci sequence#Binet's formula|Binet formula]]
<math display=block>T_{n+1} =a \tau^n +b \beta^n +c \gamma^n ,</math>
with real {{tmath|a}} and conjugates {{tmath|b}} and {{tmath|c}} the roots of <math>44y^3 -2y -1 =0.</math>

Since <math> \left\vert b \beta^n +c \gamma^n \right\vert < \tfrac25</math>, the number {{tmath|T_n}} is the [[nearest integer function|nearest integer]] to {{tmath| \,a\,\tau^{n-1} }}, with {{tmath|n > 0}} and coefficient <math>a =\tau^2 /(\tau^3 +\tau +2) =</math> {{gaps|0.33622|81169|94941|09422|53629...}}&nbsp;{{efn|Constant 𝑎 comes from [http://www.plouffe.fr Simon Plouffe's 1992 formula], its minimal polynomial can be found with an [[integer relation algorithm]].}}

The tribonacci numbers are obtained as integral powers {{tmath|n \ge 2}} of [[companion matrix]] {{tmath|Q}} to [[characteristic polynomial]] {{tmath|f}} with dominant [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors#Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices|eigenvalue]] {{tmath|\tau}}&nbsp;<ref>{{OEIS|A000073}}</ref>
<math display=block> Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} </math>
By the [[Cayley–Hamilton theorem]],
<math display=block> Q^n = \begin{pmatrix}  T_{n+2} & T_{n+1} +T_{n} & T_{n+1} \\ T_{n+1} & T_{n} +T_{n-1} & T_{n} \\ T_{n} & T_{n-1} +T_{n-2} & T_{n-1} \end{pmatrix} </math>

The [[Trace (linear algebra)#Relationship to eigenvalues|trace]] of {{tmath|Q^n }} gives the tribonacci-Lucas numbers 3, 1, 3, 7, 11, 21, 39, 71, 131, 241, 443, 815, 1499, 2757,... satisfying the same recurrence relation. Variously, <math> L_n =\lfloor \tau^n \rceil \text{ for } n >3.</math> {{OEIS|A001644}}

These Lucas numbers have the [[Fermat's little theorem|Fermat property]]: if p is prime, <math> L_{p} \equiv L_1 \bmod p .</math> The converse does not hold, but the small number of tribonacci [[pseudoprime]]s <math>\,n \mid (L_n -1)</math> makes the sequence special. The only composite numbers below {{math|10{{sup|7}} }} to pass the test are n = 182, 25201, 233{{sup|2}}, 63618, 194390, 750890, 804055, 1889041, 2487941, 3542533, 3761251, 6829689. {{OEIS|A371805}}

The tribonacci word sequence on the alphabet {{tmath|\{a,b,c\} }} is defined by the [[Semi-Thue system|substitution rule]]
<math display=block>\begin{cases}
 a \;\mapsto \;ab \\
 b \;\mapsto \;ac \\
 c \;\mapsto \;a \end{cases}</math>
With initiator {{tmath|w_0{{=}}c}}, the first seven words are
<math display=block> c,a,ab,ab.ac,abac.aba,abacaba.abacab,abacabaabacab.abacabaabac </math>
For {{tmath|n \ge 3}}, the series of words {{tmath|w_n}} produced by [[iteration|iterating]] the substitution are similarly obtained by [[Concatenation|concatenating]] the previous three: <math> w_n =w_{n-1} +w_{n-2} +w_{n-3}.</math> The number of {{math|''c'', ''b'' and ''a's''}} in each word is equal to successive tribonacci numbers and the word length {{tmath|1=l(w_n) =T_{n+2} }}.<ref>{{OEIS|A080843}}</ref>
The tribonacci word sequence is the basis of the construction of the classic [[Rauzy fractal]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Siegel |first1=Anne |last2=Thuswaldner |first2=Jörg M. |date=2009 |title=Topological properties of Rauzy fractals |url=http://numdam.org/item/MSMF_2009_2_118__1_0/ |journal=Mémoires de la Société Mathématique de France |volume=118 |series=2 |pages=1–140 |doi=10.24033/msmf.430}}</ref>

The [[Ducci sequence|four-number game]] played with sets {{tmath|S_0}} of successive tribonacci numbers {{tmath| \{ T_{n-3},T_{n-2},T_{n-1},T_n \} }}, and [[Cyclic permutation|circular shifts]] or reflections thereof, results in subsequent maximum run lengths <math> l(S_0) =3\lfloor \tfrac{n-1}{2} \rfloor,</math> {{tmath|n \ge 3}}. A game of infinite length is obtained by taking real elements <math> S_0 =\{ 1,\tau,\tau^2,\tau^3 \},</math> given to unlimited precision.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Webb |first=William A. |title=The length of the four-number game |url=https://www.fq.math.ca/Scanned/20-1/webb.pdf |journal=[[Fibonacci Quarterly]] |volume=20 | issue=1 |pages=33–35 |date=February 1982 |doi=10.1080/00150517.1982.12430025}}</ref>

==Tribonacci spiral==
[[File:Tribonacci_spiral.svg |thumb |upright=1.5 |Tribonacci spirals with different initial radii on a {{math|τ}}− rectangle.]]
A tribonacci spiral is a [[logarithmic spiral]] that gets wider by a factor of {{tmath|\tau}} for every quarter turn. It is described by the [[polar equation]] <math>r( \theta) =a \exp(k \theta),</math> with initial radius {{tmath|a}} and parameter <math>k =\frac{2}{\pi} \ln( \tau).</math>

If drawn on a tribonacci rectangle, the spiral has its pole at the foot of altitude of a triangle on the diagonal and passes through vertices of rectangles with aspect ratio {{tmath|\tau(\tau -1)}} which are perpendicularly aligned and successively scaled by a factor {{tmath|\tau^{-1} }}. The pole of the spiral divides the main diagonal in ratio {{tmath|\tau^2}} and [[Bisection|bisects]] the diagonal of the lower right rectangle.

==See also==
Solutions of equations similar to <math>x^3 =x^2 +x +1</math>:
* [[Golden ratio]] – the positive solution of the equation <math>x^2 =x +1</math>
* [[Plastic ratio]] – the real solution of the equation <math>x^3 =x +1</math>
* [[Supergolden ratio]] – the real solution of the equation <math>x^3 =x^2 +1</math>
